source_text: Constat tamen accusatorem nostrum in eodem, quem aversatur luto volvi. Cum enim confinxerit iuste redditam libidinis poenam, et hanc iustitiam divinae inculcat convenire sententiae, in prolatione autem sententiae opus Dei esse non denegat, ex qua libidinem evenisse dicit, quam erubescendam fatetur; in operam nimirum Dei, illum, quem propulsaverat, reduxit pudorem.
pass_a_gloss: It stands nevertheless that our accuser is rolled in the same mud which he turns from. For when he has feigned that the penalty of lust was justly rendered, and he impresses that this justice suits the divine sentence, but in the bringing forth of the sentence he does not deny that there is a work of God, from which he says lust came, which he confesses must be blushed at; he has brought back into the work of God that modesty which he had driven off.

lemmas.lexica: LS libido; Blaise pudenda libido vs nuptiae
LS opus; Blaise God's works vs devil's

pass_b_english: It is nevertheless clear that my accuser is rolling in the very mud he recoils from. For he has invented the claim that the punishment of lust was justly imposed, and insists that this justice belongs to the divine sentence. Yet he does not deny that the pronouncement of the sentence is God’s work. He says lust, which he admits is shameful, arose from that sentence. He has therefore brought back into God’s work the very shame he had driven away.

choices.why: Julian's pudenda libido is the appetite accompanying union, not a created substance of sin.
Julian's forensic virtue that renders to each his own, without fraude or gratia (partiality).
rejected: righteousness (Pauline overlay unless the verse forces it)

choices.why: Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
